newsitem.title: CHINA: China cadmium consumption seen rising until 2000.
newsitem.headline: China cadmium consumption seen rising until 2000.

text.p: Chinese annual consumption of cadmium is likely to rise by up to 200 tonnes a year until 2000 from more than 1,300 tonnes in 1995, a Hong Kong-based official of Sogem (Far East) Ltd said on Tuesday.

Cadmium consumption had been boosted by rising production of nickel cadmium batteries, a sector expected to grow at more than 10 percent a year for the next couple of years, Sogem's David Fong told a metals conference in Beijing.
Sogem is the trading arm of Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA.

"(Cadmium) consumption is likely to increase by 150 tonnes to 200 tonnes a year until the end of the decade," Fong said, adding that China was unlikely to begin recycling nickel cadmium in the next few years.
Chinese production of cadmium, used in some low-melting alloys, electroplating and batteries, hit 1,640 tonnes in 1995, up from 1,610 tonnes the year before, he said.
In the first eight months of 1996, China had become a net importer, with exports of 73 tonnes outweighed by imports of 631 tonnes, he said.
Exports last year totalled 1,449 tonnes compared with imports of 607 tonnes, he said.
There was still a quality gap between local and imported cadmium, with Chinese battery exporters tending to prefer to buy imports, he said without giving details.
